items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: when I got with Buddy's band, he had this boy Buddy Manatee playing banjo, Chester Zardas, bass.

ctx.x: Do you remember any outstanding men that played with Gus? No. That's new to me. I just, I'd like to trace him down. I could, he might still be around.

Who else was in Buddy's band? Did you have the... Well Buddy, let's see, when I got with Buddy's band, he had this boy Buddy Manatee playing banjo, Chester Zardas, bass. Faiso was the drummer, George Washington, trombone. He was, we had now played on bass, trombone. Buddy was on.

items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1970-02-14
items.q: And Buddy had a pretty nice band. It was George Washington on trombone, and he had Faiso on drums. Then you had Edmund Hall on clarinet, and Buddy Petit was playing the trumpet.

ctx.x: This is February the 14th, 1970. Yes, Ray. And we're interviewing Tester Zardes, and we're in Preservation Hall. Yes, Ray. All right, Tester, well, one of the main things I wanted to ask you about was when you were playing in Over the Lake, in the early 20s or whenever it was, with Buddy Petit. Yeah, 19, 20, that's right. Okay, well, now, can you tell me everything you can remember about that, how you met Buddy and what way you would play and who else was in the band and generally all kinds of things like that. I…

Well, you see, the way we started off, I was playing with a band out of, you know, around here in town until I got professional. I didn't get professional until I got with Buddy's band, you know what I mean? And Buddy had a pretty nice band. It was George Washington on trombone, and he had Faiso on drums. Then you had Edmund Hall on clarinet, and Buddy Petit was playing the trumpet. See? We didn't have, but there were six pieces, you know? Yeah. You know? And this boy, Hall, Hall was a pretty nice, you know, nice…

items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: And you take like this boy Hall. Hall used to be a terrible man. See? And by being together, working together so long

ctx.x: And the clarinet was similar to the style they used today? Just like the, yeah. Similar to George Lewis? George Lewis, yeah. Of course we still hear Edmund Hall still plays. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Never changed his style much either I guess. I don't know.

Well like I said, these fellas they've all been together, you know what I mean? And you take like this boy Hall. Hall used to be a terrible man. See? And by being together, working together so long, you know, and different things like that.

He's still real good I think. He still plays good I think. Yeah, George plays nice. I mean Edmund Hall. I haven't heard him for three years. You got one of his records, didn't you? Yeah. I was going to ask, did you always use four strings on your bass or sometimes three? Always did use four strings. Have you ever used a three?
